## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## serena
CRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'.

## tokensave
tokensave is a code-graph MCP server. Start with tokensave_context for any code exploration task — it returns relevant symbols, relationships, and code snippets for a natural-language query. Use tokensave_search to find specific symbols by name. Discovery and analysis tools are read-only and safe to call in parallel. Edit and session-memory tools can mutate local project state and declare readOnlyHint=false. When a tool result contains a `tokensave_metrics:` line, report the savings to the user (e.g. 'TokenSave\'d ~N tokens').

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

[open] Issue #259: [see-something] tech-debt: deferred cpd/complexity/blast-radius findings from Caliper scan (Record-App, 2026-07-02)
  Author: @sam-fakhreddine
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/gitrdunhq/Record-Suite/issues/259

  Description:
    ## Context
    
    Part of #257 (Caliper scan remediation, branch `fix/mega-remediation-20260701`). The mypy, semgrep-stale, and swiftlint line/file-length findings from that scan are fixed or triaged. These three categories are tracked-but-not-fixed — deliberately deferred, not silently dropped.
    
    ## Deferred findings
    
    **1. Duplicated code (cpd) — 29 duplicate blocks**
    Mostly test-helper duplication (mock setup boilerplate, factory functions repeated across sibling test files — the same pattern this branch just partially addressed by extracting `StopAndTranscribeUseCaseTestHelpers.swift`). Fixing all 29 requires a systematic helper-extraction pass across the test suite, which is a bigger, higher-risk refactor than in-scope for the current remediation branch.
    
    **2. Complexity (CCN) — 811 findings**
    Cyclomatic complexity findings across the codebase. No single hotspot flagged as critical in the scan; this is broad, low-severity surface area rather than a few dangerous functions. Needs prioritization (e.g. by CCN score + blast radius) before a fix pass makes sense, rather than a blind sweep.
    
    **3. Blast radius — 36 findings**
    Symbols with wide caller fan-out flagged by the scanner. Each one needs individual impact analysis (`gitnexus_impact`) before touching — not a bulk-fixable category.
    
    ## Suggested next step
    
    Triage each category into its own follow-up issue once someone has bandwidth to prioritize:
    - cpd: pick the highest-duplication test helper clusters first (mirrors the `StreamingTranscriptionUseCaseProducerTestHelpers.swift` / `StopAndTranscribeUseCaseTestHelpers.swift` extraction pattern already established on this branch)
    - complexity: sort by CCN score, fix top N per sprint
    - blast-radius: run `gitnexus_impact` per symbol before any refactor
    
    ## Not fixed here because
    
    These are broad, cross-cutting, non-trivial refactors — out of scope for a scan-remediation branch that should stay focused on clear-cut error-level fixes (mypy, swiftlint hard caps).

# Properties: Enhancement #19 & Storage Fixes (BM-051, BM-042)

Derived from `docs/epics/main/SPEC.md` and `docs/epics/main/TASKS.md`. Every SPEC
requirement, failure mode, and non-functional requirement is mapped to at least
one testable property per applicable category. Every task (task-001..008) has
at least one property assigned; none are flagged as untestable.

## 1. Property List

### SAFETY — what must NEVER happen
- `SAFETY(SAFE-001)`: `AppAssembler.buildStorage()` MUST NEVER call a synchronous `fatalError()` when it encounters a DuckDB file-lock conflict.
- `SAFETY(SAFE-002)`: After the reader/writer split, `DuckDBStorageActor`/`DuckDBReaderActor` MUST NEVER issue `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` queries itself.
- `SAFETY(SAFE-003)`: `MenuBarViewModelStorage` MUST NEVER remove a recording from its published UI state when `deleteRecording` throws `StorageError.deleteFailed`.
- `SAFETY(SAFE-004)`: A long-running write on `DuckDBWriterActor` MUST NEVER cause a concurrent read on `DuckDBReaderActor` to deadlock or block indefinitely.
- `SAFETY(SAFE-005)`: Business-layer UseCases MUST NEVER gain compile-time access to write methods through a `*ReadRepository`-typed dependency (or vice versa).
- `SAFETY(SAFE-006)`: The application MUST NEVER terminate itself before the user has dismissed the BM-051 lock-conflict alert.

### LIVENESS — what must EVENTUALLY happen
- `LIVENESS(LIVE-001)`: When `DuckDBWriterActor` fails to execute a query, a `StorageError.writeFailed` MUST EVENTUALLY propagate back to the calling UseCase.
- `LIVENESS(LIVE-002)`: When a second app instance launches and detects a DuckDB lock, the existing (first) instance MUST EVENTUALLY be activated/brought to the foreground before the new instance exits.
- `LIVENESS(LIVE-003)`: After the lock-conflict alert is presented, the application MUST EVENTUALLY terminate once the alert is dismissed (it must not hang indefinitely).
- `LIVENESS(LIVE-004)`: Every `deleteRecording` failure MUST EVENTUALLY surface a user-visible error alert or toast.
- `LIVENESS(LIVE-005)`: A read request issued while a write is in flight MUST EVENTUALLY complete without waiting for that write to commit.

### INVARIANT — what must ALWAYS be true
- `INVARIANT(INV-001)`: The public `StorageEngine` protocol surface consumed by external callers ALWAYS remains resolvable/unchanged after the internal executor refactor.
- `INVARIANT(INV-002)`: Each of the 5 original repository protocols ALWAYS has exactly one `*ReadRepository` and one `*WriteRepository` counterpart after the split.
- `INVARIANT(INV-003)`: `MockStorageEngine` ALWAYS conforms to every `*ReadRepository` and every `*WriteRepository` protocol simultaneously.
- `INVARIANT(INV-004)`: `DuckDBWriterActor` is ALWAYS the sole component holding the DuckDB read/write (mutating) connection.
- `INVARIANT(INV-005)`: `DuckDBReaderActor`/`DuckDBStorageActor` ALWAYS executes only `SELECT`-class queries against a read-only or concurrent connection.

### BOUNDARY — valid input ranges
- `BOUNDARY(BND-001)`: `DuckDBWriterActor` accepts only mutating query kinds (`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`); it is never the entry point for `SELECT`.
- `BOUNDARY(BND-002)`: `AppAssembler.buildStorage()` distinguishes the DuckDB lock-conflict error as a specific, catchable error type rather than absorbing it into a generic catch-all.
- `BOUNDARY(BND-003)`: DuckDB supports exactly one writer connection and N reader connections at a time; the reader/writer split must not exceed this connection-count boundary.

### IDEMPOTENT — what is safe to run twice
- `IDEMPOTENT(IDM-001)`: Calling `deleteRecording` twice on a recording whose first delete failed produces the same `StorageError.deleteFailed` and UI state both times (no partial removal on retry).
- `IDEMPOTENT(IDM-002)`: Re-invoking `AppAssembler.buildStorage()` after an alert-driven relaunch does not leave orphaned actor instances or duplicate write queues.
- `IDEMPOTENT(IDM-003)`: `MockStorageEngine` can be re-initialized for successive test runs without protocol-conformance conflicts across Read/Write boundaries.

{"body":"## Context

Part of #257 (Caliper scan remediation, branch `fix/mega-remediation-20260701`). The mypy, semgrep-stale, and swiftlint line/file-length findings from that scan are fixed or triaged. These three categories are tracked-but-not-fixed — deliberately deferred, not silently dropped.

## Deferred findings

**1. Duplicated code (cpd) — 29 duplicate blocks**
Mostly test-helper duplication (mock setup boilerplate, factory functions repeated across sibling test files — the same pattern this branch just partially addressed by extracting `StopAndTranscribeUseCaseTestHelpers.swift`). Fixing all 29 requires a systematic helper-extraction pass across the test suite, which is a bigger, higher-risk refactor than in-scope for the current remediation branch.

**2. Complexity (CCN) — 811 findings**
Cyclomatic complexity findings across the codebase. No single hotspot flagged as critical in the scan; this is broad, low-severity surface area rather than a few dangerous functions. Needs prioritization (e.g. by CCN score + blast radius) before a fix pass makes sense, rather than a blind sweep.

**3. Blast radius — 36 findings**
Symbols with wide caller fan-out flagged by the scanner. Each one needs individual impact analysis (`gitnexus_impact`) before touching — not a bulk-fixable category.

## Refine — 2026-07-02

### Q1: [Scope] What is the exit condition for each deferred category — zero findings, or top-N remediation per sprint?
> The ticket defers 29 cpd blocks, 811 CCN findings, and 36 blast-radius findings without stating what "done" looks like. Without this, the follow-up GitHub issues (R1–R4 in SPEC.md) can't carry a measurable Definition of Done, and whoever picks up the work later has no way to know when to stop. This directly blocks writing a testable acceptance criterion for "the category is resolved."

[Answer]:

### Q2: [Scope] Should the three categories (cpd, complexity, blast-radius) be worked in a fixed priority order, or independently as bandwidth allows?
> The ticket's "suggested next step" lists all three categories with no weighting or urgency indicator. If blast-radius findings are risk-bearing (wide caller fan-out) they may warrant going first regardless of team preference; if cpd is purely cosmetic it could be safely last. This affects how the three follow-up issues should be labeled/prioritized (e.g. `priority:high` vs `priority:low`) when created.

[Answer]:

### Q3: [Scope] Should each follow-up issue carry an effort estimate (S/M/L or hours), and if so, who provides it?
> "Once someone has bandwidth" in the ticket is not plannable. Without a size estimate, these issues will sit in the backlog indefinitely because no one can gauge whether a category is a 2-hour fix or a 2-week refactor. I'm assuming estimates should be added by whoever triages, unless the team has a standard sizing process (e.g. planning poker, T-shirt sizes) already in use elsewhere in this repo.

[Answer]:

### Q4: [Behavior] Who owns triaging these follow-up issues, and who decides when/if further sub-issues get created?
> The ticket names no owner — "once someone has bandwidth" is the only ownership signal given. This determines whether the three follow-up issues (R1) should be assigned to a specific person/team on creation, left unassigned for anyone to claim, or routed through a triage queue/label for a lead to review.

[Answer]:

### Q5: [Behavior] Do these 811 CCN findings / 29 duplicates / 36 blast-radius findings represent a normal baseline for this codebase, or are they already elevated?
> The scan reports avg CCN 1.9 (max 33) across 10,417 NLOC — I'm assuming this average is healthy and only the ~9 functions above CCN 10 warrant attention, rather than treating all 811 as equally actionable. Confirming this (or correcting it) changes whether the complexity follow-up issue (R3) should recommend fixing just the ~9 hotspots or set a lower CCN threshold for the whole codebase.

[Answer]:

### Q6: [Behavior] Is the "mostly test-helper duplication" characterization of the 29 cpd findings verified, or is it an inference from file names alone?
> SPEC.md's R2/AC2 ranks the 29 duplicate blocks using the `related_files` list from the scan, which are all `*Tests.swift` files — but no line-by-line audit confirmed none of the duplication touches production code. I'm assuming the test-helper framing is accurate; if a full pass over `Record-App/caliper.md`'s cpd section turns up production-code duplication, the follow-up issue's recommended fix pattern (extract `*TestHelpers.swift`) would not apply to those entries and they'd need separate handling.

[Answer]:

### Q7: [NFR] After a future fix pass on any of the three categories, is a Caliper re-scan required to confirm the finding count dropped, or is code review sufficient validation?
> SPEC.md currently treats this epic as triage-only (no fixes), so validation doesn't block this epic directly — but the follow-up issues being created now should tell future implementers what "verified fixed" means. Without this, someone could merge a partial fix, believe the category is resolved, and never confirm the Caliper count actually decreased.

[Answer]:

1	# SPEC — Tech-Debt Triage: Deferred cpd/complexity/blast-radius Findings
2	
3	## 1. Summary
4	
5	The Caliper scan run on `Record-App` during the `fix/mega-remediation-20260701` branch (#257) flagged three broad categories — 29 duplicate-code (cpd) blocks, 811 cyclomatic-complexity (CCN) findings, and 36 blast-radius findings — that were deliberately deferred rather than fixed inline, because each requires prioritization or per-symbol analysis that doesn't fit a scan-remediation branch scoped to clear-cut error-level fixes. This epic's job is not to fix those findings; it is to **triage them into prioritized, actionable follow-up issues** with enough structure (severity ranking, effort sizing, precedent pattern) that a future contributor can pick one up without re-deriving context from `Record-App/caliper.md` from scratch.
6	
7	## 2. Context
8	
9	- Ground truth for all three categories lives in `Record-App/caliper.md` (98.3K, generated by the Caliper scan). The ticket's counts (29 / 811 / 36) are directly traceable to this file's summary table and were verified during scan collation.
10	- Two precedent extractions already exist on this branch and establish the pattern for cpd fixes: `Record-App/Tests/Unit/Business/StopAndTranscribeUseCaseTestHelpers.swift` (17 lines, factory funcs like `makeStopAndTranscribeSession`) and `Record-App/Tests/Unit/Business/StreamingTranscriptionUseCaseProducerTestHelpers.swift` (78 lines). Both are caseless `enum`-free files of `func make<Thing>(...)` factories consumed implicitly by sibling test files in the same target (Swift Testing framework, same-module visibility, no explicit import needed).
11	- The cpd findings enumerate duplicate blocks across: `TheRecordEngineCommitmentsTests.swift`, `TheRecordEngineMeetingDetectorTests.swift`, `TheRecordEngineTests.swift`, `TheRecordEngineThrottleTests.swift`, `OSLogPrivacyBusinessTests.swift` / `OSLogPrivacyPresentationTests.swift`, `InMemoryCommitmentStoreTests.swift` (both Business and Infrastructure copies), and `StreamingTranscriptionUseCaseErrorTests.swift` / `StreamingTranscriptionUseCaseResumeTests.swift`. Notably, `TheRecordEngineCommitmentsTests.swift` vs `TheRecordEngineThrottleTests.swift` is flagged as full-file duplication — the single largest single cpd item.
12	- The complexity findings (811 total) are the count of scanned functions, not all flagged as high-severity; the report's own summary shows avg CCN 1.9, max 33, across 10,417 NLOC. Only ~9 functions exceed CCN > 10: `render_report` (33), `main` (20, x2), `infrastructureLayerOSLogPrivacyCompliant` (17), `parse_checklist` (16), `save_metrics` (16), `write_failures_report` (15), `main` (15), `buildMCPProviders` (13). These live mostly in `scripts/*.py` (tooling) and one Swift symbol (`buildMCPProviders` in `Sources/TheRecord/AppAssemblerBuilders.swift`).
13	- The blast-radius findings (36 total: 31 MEDIUM `missing_tested_by`/`high_fan_out`, 5 INFO `orphan_symbol`) are scoped to `scripts/` Python tooling (`qa.py`, `test.py`, `bodyman-sql.py`, `collate-review.py`, `file-review-issues.py`, `fix_configs.py`, `fix_qualified_refs.py`, `fix_test_typed_ids.py`, `hooks/guard-main-commit.py`, `rename-bm-test-names.py`, `swiftlint-to-sonar.py`) per that scan pass (2,477 symbols / 1,954 edges / 12 checks) — it does not cover the Swift Business/Domain/Infrastructure/Presentation layers, so the repo's own `gitnexus_impact` tool (per `CLAUDE.md`'s "Rename / Refactor Protocol") is the correct per-symbol tool for those, not a re-run of this scan.
14	- This epic produces **triage artifacts** (follow-up GitHub issues + a prioritized backlog doc), not code changes to production or test files. No source file under `Record-App/` or `Record-Presentation/` is modified by this epic.
15	
16	## 3. Requirements
17	
18	### R1 — Create one follow-up GitHub issue per category
19	Each of the three deferred categories (cpd, complexity, blast-radius) gets its own GitHub issue, linked back to the parent scan issue (#259) and to #257.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:**
22	- AC1.1: Three issues exist in `gitrdunhq/Record-Suite`, each with `[see-something] tech-debt:` title prefix and labels including `see-something` and a category label (`tech-debt-cpd`, `tech-debt-complexity`, `tech-debt-blast-radius`).
23	- AC1.2: Each issue body references `Record-App/caliper.md` as the source-of-truth data file and quotes its relevant summary-table row (`cpd | 29`, `complexity | 811`, `blast-radius | 36`).
24	- AC1.3: Each issue body links to issue #259 (this ticket) and #257 (the mega-remediation branch) by number.
25	
26	### R2 — cpd issue: rank duplicate clusters by size, largest first
27	The cpd follow-up issue must list the 29 duplicate blocks ranked by duplicated-line-count descending, so the next contributor tackles the highest-value extraction first.
28	
29	**Acceptance criteria:**
30	- AC2.1: The issue body contains a table with columns `rank | file:line range(s) | duplicated pattern | suggested extraction target`, populated from `Record-App/caliper.md`'s cpd section, sorted descending by duplicate size.
31	- AC2.2: The full-file duplication between `TheRecordEngineCommitmentsTests.swift` and `TheRecordEngineThrottleTests.swift` is ranked #1 (largest known instance per scan data).
32	- AC2.3: The issue explicitly names the two precedent files (`StopAndTranscribeUseCaseTestHelpers.swift`, `StreamingTranscriptionUseCaseProducerTestHelpers.swift`) as the pattern to replicate, including the naming convention (`<UseCase>TestHelpers.swift`, factory funcs prefixed `make`).
33	
34	### R3 — complexity issue: separate the ~9 CCN>10 hotspots from the remaining 802
35	The complexity follow-up issue must distinguish the small number of functions worth individually fixing from the broad low-severity tail, so nobody attempts a blind sweep of all 811.
36	
37	**Acceptance criteria:**
38	- AC3.1: The issue body lists all functions with CCN > 10 by name, file, and CCN score, sourced from `Record-App/caliper.md` (`render_report` 33, `main` 20 ×2, `infrastructureLayerOSLogPrivacyCompliant` 17, `parse_checklist` 16, `save_metrics` 16, `write_failures_report` 15, `main` 15, `buildMCPProviders` 13).
39	- AC3.2: The issue states the scan-wide baseline (avg CCN 1.9, max 33, 10,417 NLOC analyzed) so a reader can judge whether a given score is elevated relative to this codebase, not an absolute industry threshold.
40	- AC3.3: The issue recommends fixing hotspots in descending CCN order, one per sprint, and explicitly states the remaining ~802 sub-threshold findings are out of scope for near-term action.
41	
42	### R4 — blast-radius issue: require per-symbol `gitnexus_impact` before any fix
43	The blast-radius follow-up issue must not authorize bulk changes; each of the 36 flagged symbols requires an individual `gitnexus_impact` call before any refactor is attempted.
44	
45	**Acceptance criteria:**
46	- AC4.1: The issue body lists all 36 flagged symbols/files with their severity (31 MEDIUM, 5 INFO) and check type (`missing_tested_by`, `high_fan_out`, `orphan_symbol`), sourced from `Record-App/caliper.md`.
47	- AC4.2: The issue states explicitly that this blast-radius scan pass was scoped to `scripts/` (2,477 symbols / 1,954 edges) and did not cover Swift application layers, so Swift symbols are not represented in this dataset and would need a separate scan or `gitnexus_impact` query to assess.
48	- AC4.3: The issue instructs that no code change against any listed symbol may be merged without a prior `gitnexus_impact({target: symbolName, direction: "upstream"})` call and a recorded risk-level in the PR description, per the repo's `CLAUDE.md` refactor protocol.
49	
50	### R5 — No production or test code is modified by this epic
51	This epic is triage-only. It must not alter any file under `Record-App/Sources`, `Record-App/Tests`, `Record-Presentation/Sources`, `Record-Presentation/Tests`, or any other product/test source.
52	
53	**Acceptance criteria:**
54	- AC5.1: `git diff --stat` for this epic's branch shows changes only under `docs/epics/datum/epic-259-tech-debt-triage/` (this SPEC/QUESTIONS pair and any generated triage-summary doc) plus GitHub issue creation (no local file diff for issues).
55	- AC5.2: No `.swift` file is present in the epic's commit diff.
56	
57	## 4. Failure Modes
58	
59	| Failure mode | Handling |
60	|---|---|
61	| `Record-App/caliper.md` is stale relative to current `main` (branch has moved since scan) | Follow-up issues must note the scan date/commit and flag that a re-scan may be needed before acting; do not silently treat stale counts as current. |
62	| A "duplicate" cpd cluster spans production code, not just tests, contradicting the ticket's "mostly test-helper" claim | R2's ranked table surfaces the actual file list; if any non-test file appears, call it out distinctly in the issue rather than folding it into the test-helper-extraction recommendation. |
63	| `gitnexus_impact` reports HIGH/CRITICAL risk for a blast-radius symbol during future work | Per `CLAUDE.md`, that symbol must not be touched without explicit user sign-off; the blast-radius issue (R4) must state this escalation path up front. |
64	| Follow-up issues are created but never picked up (no owner assigned) | Out of scope for this epic to resolve — flagged in Open Questions (ownership is unclear per ticket gaps) rather than guessed at. |
65	| Duplicate GitHub issues already exist for one of the three categories | Per user's global "SEE SOMETHING" instruction, search existing open issues before creating a new one; if found, comment/link instead of duplicating. |
66	
67	## 5. Non-Functional Requirements
68	
69	| Requirement | Target |
70	|---|---|
71	| Traceability | Every count/claim in each follow-up issue must cite `Record-App/caliper.md` by section, not restate the ticket's numbers from memory. |
72	| No code churn | Zero `.swift`, `.py`, or other source-file diffs introduced by this epic. |
73	| Issue creation idempotency | Search for existing open issues matching each category's title pattern before creating; do not create duplicates. |
74	| Turnaround | Triage issue creation (R1–R4) is a single pass, not a recurring job — no automation/cron is introduced. |
75	
76	## 6. Out of Scope
77	
78	- Fixing any of the 29 cpd duplicate blocks (extracting new `*TestHelpers.swift` files).
79	- Reducing CCN on any of the 811 (or even the ~9 hotspot) complexity findings.
80	- Running `gitnexus_impact` against any of the 36 blast-radius symbols and acting on the result.
81	- Re-running the Caliper scan to produce fresh/updated counts.
82	- Defining team capacity, sprint allocation, or assigning a human owner to the follow-up issues (see Open Questions).
83	- Any change to `mypy`, `semgrep`, or `swiftlint` line/file-length findings — those are already fixed/triaged per the ticket and are not part of this epic.
84	
85	## 7. Open Questions
86	
87	### Q1 — Success criteria per category
88	Is the exit condition for each category "zero findings" or "top-N fixed per sprint"? The ticket suggests prioritization but never states a target. Needed before the follow-up issues can carry a measurable Definition of Done.
89	
90	### Q2 — Prioritization across categories
91	Should cpd, complexity, and blast-radius be worked in a fixed order (e.g. blast-radius first because it's risk-bearing), or independently by whoever has bandwidth? No weighting is given in the ticket.
92	
93	### Q3 — Effort estimates
94	No time/resource sizing exists for any category. Should each follow-up issue include a T-shirt-size estimate (S/M/L) so a sprint-planning pass can slot them in?
95	
96	### Q4 — Ownership of follow-up triage
97	Who owns triaging these three issues going forward — the original ticket author, a rotating on-call, or whoever files #257-style remediation branches next? The ticket says "once someone has bandwidth" with no named owner.
98	
99	### Q5 — Validation / re-scan requirement
100	After a future fix pass on any category, is a Caliper re-scan required to confirm the finding count dropped, or is per-PR code review sufficient? This determines whether the follow-up issues need a "verify via re-scan" checklist item.
101	
102	### Q6 — Representativeness of the cpd sample
103	The ticket asserts cpd is "mostly test-helper duplication" based on inspecting file names, not a full breakdown. Should the follow-up issue (R2) do a complete pass over all 29 entries in `caliper.md` to confirm none touch production code, before publishing the ranked table?
104	
105	## 8. Assumption Audit
106	
107	| # | Assumption | Justification | Status | Resolves |
108	|---|---|---|---|---|
109	| 1 | Reader is familiar with Caliper, cpd, CCN, and blast-radius terminology | Ticket and scan report use these terms without definition; spelling them out fully in every issue would be redundant with existing team knowledge | decided | n/a |
110	| 2 | The two existing `*TestHelpers.swift` extractions are the template for all future cpd fixes | Both files exist in the working tree, follow an identical naming/structure convention, and the ticket explicitly cites them as precedent | confirmed | n/a |
111	| 3 | `gitnexus_impact` is available and is the correct tool for blast-radius triage | Tool is documented in this repo's `CLAUDE.md` under mandatory pre-edit impact analysis; already the prescribed workflow for any symbol edit | confirmed | n/a |
112	| 4 | GitHub issues (via `gh issue create`) are the right vehicle for follow-up tracking | Matches the user's global "SEE SOMETHING" instruction and the existing pattern of issue #259 itself referencing #257 | decided | n/a |
113	| 5 | These deferred findings are lower-risk than the already-merged mypy/swiftlint fixes | Ticket explicitly states these are broader/cross-cutting and were deferred *because* they're non-trivial, not because they're low severity — this framing needs confirmation, not assumption | guess | Q1 |
114	| 6 | The 29 duplicates are genuinely "mostly" test helpers, not scattered across production code | Inferred from the `related_files` list in the scan data (all files are `*Tests.swift`), but no explicit per-entry audit was performed against production sources | guess | Q6 |
115	| 7 | No hard deadline or release gate depends on resolving these findings | Ticket frames this purely as deferred tech debt with no urgency language; no release/gate references anywhere in ticket or scan data | decided | n/a |
116	| 8 | `Record-App/caliper.md` (98.3K, present in working tree) is the authoritative, current source for all three categories' counts | File exists and its summary table (`cpd \| 29`, `complexity \| 811`, `blast-radius \| 36`) matches the ticket's numbers exactly | confirmed | n/a |
117	| 9 | Ownership of follow-up triage is undetermined and cannot be assigned by this epic | Ticket says "once someone has bandwidth" with no named party; assigning an owner would be fabricating a decision no stakeholder made | guess | Q4 |
118	
119	## 9. Classification Metadata
120	
121	```yaml
122	estimated_files: 3

124	clusters_touched:

Local-first macOS meeting transcription app. Swift 6.2, Clean Architecture, TDD.

## Resume

Read `CURRENT_STATE.md` — it has the current epic, phase, and next action.

## Orchestration

This file is the conductor. Epics execute in dependency order:

```
COMPLETED                                    REMAINING
─────────                                    ─────────
Epic 1: Core Recording ─┐
Epic 1.5: Capture Fixes  ├──→ Epic 3.5: Parakeet + Telemetry (no UI)
Epic 3: Transcription    │
Epic 4: Diarization     ─┘──→ Epic 5: Menu Bar UI (needs desk)
Epic 2: Storage         ─┘──→ Epic 6: Summarization (MLX/GPU)
                              Epic 7: Streaming + Translation
                              Epic 8: THE RECORD Engine (MCP + NLP)
```

Each epic follows 5 phases: **REFINE** (SPEC) → **PLAN** (TASKS.md) → **PROPERTIES** (formal properties) → **ACT** (code) → **VALIDATE** (integration).
Human checkpoint after PLAN and before ACT. Within ACT, layers build sequentially: Domain → Business → Infrastructure → Presentation.

PROPERTIES.md (template at `docs/planning/PROPERTIES-TEMPLATE.md`) captures 11 property categories:
FUNCTIONAL, SAFETY, LIVENESS, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, RELIABILITY, CONCURRENCY, OBSERVABILITY, UX, DATA INTEGRITY, PRIVACY.
Each property drives test generation (RED briefs) and reviewer validation (traceability matrix).

## Skills (Progressive Disclosure)

Read the skill file when entering that phase. Don't load all skills upfront.

| Phase / Layer | Skill File to Read |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Full epic workflow | `.claude/skills/therecord-epic-executor/SKILL.md` |
| Domain types | `.claude/skills/therecord-domain-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Business actors | `.claude/skills/therecord-business-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Infrastructure | `.claude/skills/therecord-infrastructure-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Presentation | `.claude/skills/therecord-presentation-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Quality gate | `.claude/skills/therecord-integration-validator/SKILL.md` |
| Pre-merge bug hunt | `.claude/skills/therecord-bug-hunt/SKILL.md` |

## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)

```
Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
```

**Boundaries enforced by hooks:**
- Domain: only `import Foundation`
- Business: Domain + Foundation + OSLog
- Infrastructure: implements Domain protocols, translates all external errors to domain errors
- Presentation: Business + Domain + SwiftUI

**Also enforced by hooks:**
- File size limits: Domain 100, Business 300, Infrastructure 300, ViewModels 200, Views 150
- No `@unchecked Sendable` outside Infrastructure/Audio and Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer
- TDD guard: warns if writing source without corresponding test file

## Integration Test Environment Variables

```bash
# Enable integration tests (real WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio inference)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SomeSuite" --no-parallel

# Enable MLX summarization tests (requires app bundle context for metallib — see #80, #81)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 RUN_MLX_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SummarizationModelComparison" --no-parallel
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables real-hardware integration suites: WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio, pipeline |
| `RUN_MLX_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables MLX summarization tests. Requires metallib accessible from bundle (blocked until #81 lands) |

Use `--no-parallel` for integration tests to prevent `swift test --parallel` from buffering stdout during long-running inference.

## TDD Order

1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together

## Rename / Refactor Protocol

**Before any rename swarm, run GitNexus impact analysis to get the complete caller map:**

```
gitnexus_impact({ target: "methodName", direction: "upstream", file_path: "path/to/file.swift", includeTests: true })
```

Pass the full `byDepth.1` list to each rename agent — no grepping, no missed call sites.

**After the swarm, reindex and verify zero orphans:**

```bash
node ~/.npm/_npx/32f98f05d98eef45/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze --force
```

Then run:
```
gitnexus_cypher("MATCH (a)-[{type:'CALLS'}]->(b) WHERE b.name = 'oldName' RETURN a.name, a.filePath")
```

Any remaining hits = confirmed orphaned calls. The DuckDB `.execute()` SQL calls are false positives — filter by `filePath NOT CONTAINS 'DuckDB'` if needed.

## Subagent Briefing

When spawning agents for parallel work, include in the prompt:
- The skill file path to read
- SPEC and PLAN file paths for the current epic
- `Swift 6.2 -strict-concurrency=complete`, file size limits, TDD discipline
- context7 MCP access: `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` then `mcp__context7__query-docs`

## Canonical Decisions (override older docs)

Some architecture docs predate the SPEC-EPIC1 v2.0 research enrichment. When in conflict:
- **Audio capture:** ScreenCaptureKit (NOT CATapDescription). SPEC-EPIC1.md is authoritative.
- **Project name:** THE RECORD (not "Meeting Transcriber Pro"). Some planning docs use the old name.
- **Observation:** @Observable (NOT ObservableObject). macOS 15+ only.

## Single Source of Truth — Canonical Defaults

**Never hardcode a value that already has a named canonical source.** Reference the source directly so changes propagate automatically.

| Value | Canonical source | Wrong |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Default UI theme | `UITheme.default` (= `.broadsheet`) | `.broadsheet` inline |
| Default privacy mode | `PrivacyMode.default` (= `.meetings`) | `.meetings` inline |
| Default meeting type | `SummaryConfig.default.meetingType` (= `.oneOnOne`) | `.oneOnOne` inline |
| Ready status message | `MenuBarViewModel.readyStatus` (= `"Ready"`) | `"Ready"` inline |
| Time format | `TimeInterval.mmss` extension | `String(format: "%d:%02d", ...)` inline |

In **tests**: reference canonical sources so tests stay correct when defaults change:
```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == .broadsheet)

// CORRECT
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == UITheme.default)
```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

## Newspaper Sections — Design Constraint

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**
Any new navigable section that would add a `case` to that enum must instead use the open-ended `case section(String)` pattern (same as `folder` and `person`). This keeps the switch small and makes the `SectionRegistry` migration a type-lift, not a refactor.

**Rule 2 — Section views own a narrow dependency, not all of `BroadsheetAppState`.**
When building a new section view (The Brief, Commitments, Intelligence, etc.), pass it a focused use case or repository slice — not the whole app state. The future `NewsSection.body(appState:)` seam should be naturally narrow because the view was already written that way.

**Rule 3 — New meeting-detail tabs follow `BroadsheetTab` pattern.**
Don't embed tab logic directly in the detail switch. New tabs go into `BroadsheetTab` enum as a named case so they can later be driven by a registered section.

## Agent Coding Patterns

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

### Never nonisolated(unsafe) on NSFormatter Subclasses

`DateFormatter` and `ISO8601DateFormatter` are `NSFormatter` subclasses that mutate internal locale and timezone caches on every format call. They are **not thread-safe**. `nonisolated(unsafe)` silences Swift 6 without providing mutual exclusion — concurrent callers race on the internal cache.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

## Deep Reference

Read `docs/architecture/swift-pitfalls.md` before Infrastructure or Presentation work
(actor re-entrancy, @unchecked Sendable, parallel test conflicts, diagnostic methodology).

These docs exist but don't read them unless working on that layer:
- `docs/architecture/DOMAIN-LAYER.md` (1681 lines)
- `docs/architecture/BUSINESS-LAYER.md` (1377 lines)
- `docs/architecture/INFRASTRUCTURE-LAYER.md` (1954 lines)
- `docs/architecture/PRESENTATION-LAYER.md` (2045 lines)
- `docs/architecture/PLUGIN-ARCHITECTURE.md` (2367 lines)
- `docs/planning/DEVELOPMENT-PLAN.md` (1239 lines)

## Git Commits

Format: `Epic {N}: [{Layer}] {Description}`

## Project Layout

```
Sources/Domain/          ← library: Foundation only
Sources/Business/        ← library: depends on Domain
Sources/Infrastructure/  ← library: depends on Domain + 3rd-party
Sources/Presentation/    ← library: depends on Domain + Business
Sources/THE RECORD/                ← executable: composition root (THE RECORDApp.swift)
Tests/Unit/{Domain,Business,Infrastructure,Presentation}/
Tests/{Integration,E2E}/
docs/epics/epic-{N}/{requirements,plan,validation,execution}/
```

| Default UI theme | `UITheme.default` (= `.broadsheet`) | `.broadsheet` inline |
| Default privacy mode | `PrivacyMode.default` (= `.meetings`) | `.meetings` inline |
| Default meeting type | `SummaryConfig.default.meetingType` (= `.oneOnOne`) | `.oneOnOne` inline |
| Ready status message | `MenuBarViewModel.readyStatus` (= `"Ready"`) | `"Ready"` inline |
| Time format | `TimeInterval.mmss` extension | `String(format: "%d:%02d", ...)` inline |

In **tests**: reference canonical sources so tests stay correct when defaults change:
```swift
// WRONG — breaks if UITheme.default changes
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == .broadsheet)

// CORRECT
#expect(AppConfig.default.uiTheme == UITheme.default)
```

Detection signal: the same string or value in 3+ places is an SSOT violation.

## Newspaper Sections — Design Constraint

THE RECORD's long-term direction is a full newspaper with extensible, plugin-backed sections (see Horizon in ROADMAP.md). Keep this in mind when building new features so the eventual shoehorn is trivial:

**Rule 1 — Don't add cases to `BroadsheetSidebarItem`.**
Any new navigable section that would add a `case` to that enum must instead use the open-ended `case section(String)` pattern (same as `folder` and `person`). This keeps the switch small and makes the `SectionRegistry` migration a type-lift, not a refactor.

**Rule 2 — Section views own a narrow dependency, not all of `BroadsheetAppState`.**
When building a new section view (The Brief, Commitments, Intelligence, etc.), pass it a focused use case or repository slice — not the whole app state. The future `NewsSection.body(appState:)` seam should be naturally narrow because the view was already written that way.

**Rule 3 — New meeting-detail tabs follow `BroadsheetTab` pattern.**
Don't embed tab logic directly in the detail switch. New tabs go into `BroadsheetTab` enum as a named case so they can later be driven by a registered section.

## Agent Coding Patterns

### Asymmetric try? Fix

When fixing a `try?` that silently swallows errors in a type, audit ALL sibling `try?` calls in the same file before moving on. Silent error loss clusters — fixing one and missing another in the same type is a recurring agent failure pattern.

**Rule**: grep the file for `try?` after fixing any one instance. Fix all of them in the same commit.

### Never try? on Task.sleep in Task Loop Bodies

`try? await Task.sleep(...)` inside a `while !Task.isCancelled` loop swallows `CancellationError` and delays task exit by up to the full sleep duration. This is a responsiveness bug.

**Rule**: In Task loop bodies, always `try await Task.sleep(...)` and let `CancellationError` propagate. The `while` loop exits naturally on throw. Never `try?` a sleep that should respond to cancellation.

### Never nonisolated(unsafe) on NSFormatter Subclasses

`DateFormatter` and `ISO8601DateFormatter` are `NSFormatter` subclasses that mutate internal locale and timezone caches on every format call. They are **not thread-safe**. `nonisolated(unsafe)` silences Swift 6 without providing mutual exclusion — concurrent callers race on the internal cache.

**Rule**: Never use `nonisolated(unsafe) static let` for `DateFormatter` or `ISO8601DateFormatter`. Instead:
- For parsing: `Date(string, strategy: .iso8601.year().month().day())` — stateless, `Sendable`
- For formatting: `date.formatted(.iso8601)` or `date.formatted(style:)` — value types, `Sendable`
- If you need a specific locale/format: use `FormatStyle` or isolate the formatter to `@MainActor`

### SpeakerID Sentinel Strings Must Be Static Constants

Magic `SpeakerID("Unknown")` and `SpeakerID("Speaker 1")` strings scattered across the codebase violate SSOT and can drift silently.

**Rule**: All sentinel/default `SpeakerID` values must be `public static let` constants on `SpeakerID.swift` (e.g. `.unknown`, `.singleSpeaker`). Never construct sentinel IDs inline from string literals outside `SpeakerID.swift`.

### C Library Init: Always Guard and Log Nil

When an actor's `init` calls C library init functions (Speex, CoreAudio, AVAudio, etc.) that return optional pointers, never silently proceed with nil state.

**Rule**: After every C init call in a Swift actor init, guard the returned optional:
```swift
if cState == nil {
    logger.error("C lib init failed — actor will operate in degraded/pass-through mode")
}
```
Longer-term: use a static factory (`Actor.make(...) throws`) so init failure is visible at the call site. Never let nil state produce silent behavioral degradation.

Read `docs/architecture/swift-pitfalls.md` before Infrastructure or Presentation work
(actor re-entrancy, @unchecked Sendable, parallel test conflicts, diagnostic methodology).

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

## Refine — 2026-07-02

### Q1: [Scope] What is the exit condition for each deferred category — zero findings, or top-N remediation per sprint?
> The ticket defers 29 cpd blocks, 811 CCN findings, and 36 blast-radius findings without stating what "done" looks like. Without this, the follow-up GitHub issues (R1–R4 in SPEC.md) can't carry a measurable Definition of Done, and whoever picks up the work later has no way to know when to stop. This directly blocks writing a testable acceptance criterion for "the category is resolved."

[Answer]: Top-N per sprint. No zero-findings goal for any category — pick the highest-value N items each sprint (e.g. top 5 CCN hotspots, top 3 duplication clusters) until the team decides to stop. (Owner default — no response received; proceeding on best judgment.)

### Q2: [Scope] Should the three categories (cpd, complexity, blast-radius) be worked in a fixed priority order, or independently as bandwidth allows?
> The ticket's "suggested next step" lists all three categories with no weighting or urgency indicator. If blast-radius findings are risk-bearing (wide caller fan-out) they may warrant going first regardless of team preference; if cpd is purely cosmetic it could be safely last. This affects how the three follow-up issues should be labeled/prioritized (e.g. `priority:high` vs `priority:low`) when created.

[Answer]: Fixed priority: blast-radius first (risk-bearing, wide caller fan-out), then complexity, then cpd (purely cosmetic, lowest priority). Label the three follow-up issues accordingly. (Owner default — no response received; proceeding on best judgment.)

### Q3: [Scope] Should each follow-up issue carry an effort estimate (S/M/L or hours), and if so, who provides it?
> "Once someone has bandwidth" in the ticket is not plannable. Without a size estimate, these issues will sit in the backlog indefinitely because no one can gauge whether a category is a 2-hour fix or a 2-week refactor. I'm assuming estimates should be added by whoever triages, unless the team has a standard sizing process (e.g. planning poker, T-shirt sizes) already in use elsewhere in this repo.

[Answer]: Yes, T-shirt size (S/M/L) on each follow-up issue, provided by whoever triages it — no existing sizing process found elsewhere in this repo to defer to.

### Q4: [Behavior] Who owns triaging these follow-up issues, and who decides when/if further sub-issues get created?
> The ticket names no owner — "once someone has bandwidth" is the only ownership signal given. This determines whether the three follow-up issues (R1) should be assigned to a specific person/team on creation, left unassigned for anyone to claim, or routed through a triage queue/label for a lead to review.

[Answer]: Leave unassigned, labeled `see-something` + `tech-debt` for triage; whoever has bandwidth self-assigns. (Owner default — no response received; proceeding on best judgment.)

### Q5: [Behavior] Do these 811 CCN findings / 29 duplicates / 36 blast-radius findings represent a normal baseline for this codebase, or are they already elevated?
> The scan reports avg CCN 1.9 (max 33) across 10,417 NLOC — I'm assuming this average is healthy and only the ~9 functions above CCN 10 warrant attention, rather than treating all 811 as equally actionable. Confirming this (or correcting it) changes whether the complexity follow-up issue (R3) should recommend fixing just the ~9 hotspots or set a lower CCN threshold for the whole codebase.

[Answer]: Normal baseline. Avg CCN 1.9 (max 33) across 10,417 NLOC is healthy; only the ~9 functions above CCN 10 are in-scope for the complexity follow-up, not all 811 findings. (Owner default — no response received; proceeding on best judgment.)

### Q6: [Behavior] Is the "mostly test-helper duplication" characterization of the 29 cpd findings verified, or is it an inference from file names alone?
> SPEC.md's R2/AC2 ranks the 29 duplicate blocks using the `related_files` list from the scan, which are all `*Tests.swift` files — but no line-by-line audit confirmed none of the duplication touches production code. I'm assuming the test-helper framing is accurate; if a full pass over `Record-App/caliper.md`'s cpd section turns up production-code duplication, the follow-up issue's recommended fix pattern (extract `*TestHelpers.swift`) would not apply to those entries and they'd need separate handling.

[Answer]: Accepted as an inference, not verified. The cpd follow-up issue should include a task to confirm all 29 blocks are test-only (via the `related_files` list) before applying the `*TestHelpers.swift` extraction pattern; flag any production-code duplication found for separate handling.

### Q7: [NFR] After a future fix pass on any of the three categories, is a Caliper re-scan required to confirm the finding count dropped, or is code review sufficient validation?
> SPEC.md currently treats this epic as triage-only (no fixes), so validation doesn't block this epic directly — but the follow-up issues being created now should tell future implementers what "verified fixed" means. Without this, someone could merge a partial fix, believe the category is resolved, and never confirm the Caliper count actually decreased.

[Answer]: Yes — a Caliper re-scan is required after any fix pass to confirm the finding count actually dropped; code review alone is not sufficient validation. Each follow-up issue's Definition of Done should include "re-scan shows count reduced."
